Individual Values (IVs) are hidden numbers from 0–31 for each stat, randomly set when a Pokémon is generated. Think of them as genetic potential — two Pokémon of the same species at the same level can have different stats purely because of IVs. A Pokémon with 31 IV in every stat is called \"perfect\" or \"6IV.\"

Effort Values (EVs) are extra points a Pokémon earns from battling. Every 4 EVs invested in a stat adds roughly +1 point to that stat at Level 100. You can put up to 252 EVs into a single stat, and 510 total across all six — most competitive players focus EVs into just two or three stats instead of spreading them thin.

Every Pokémon also has a Nature, which boosts one stat by 10%% and lowers another by 10%% — or does nothing, for five neutral natures. Pairing the right Nature with EV investment is a core part of building a strong Pokémon.

A Pokémon\'s final stat comes from its species\' Base Stat, your chosen IV and EV, its Level, and its Nature. Try the calculator above to see how much a single stat can swing between a worst case (0 IV, 0 EV, negative Nature) and best case (31 IV, 252 EV, positive Nature) Pokémon of the same species.

Combat Power (CP) is Pokémon GO\'s single number summarizing how strong a Pokémon is right now. It\'s calculated from the species\' Attack, Defense and Stamina, its Level, and its individual IVs — a higher CP generally means a stronger Pokémon in battle.
What are IVs in Pokémon GO?

Unlike the main games (0–31), Pokémon GO IVs range from 0–15 per stat (Attack, Defense, Stamina). They\'re set randomly when you catch or hatch a Pokémon and never change afterward. A Pokémon with 15/15/15 is called \"Perfect\" or \"100%.\"
This app can\'t read your save data, so it can only estimate. To see the exact IVs of a Pokémon you\'ve caught, use the in-game Appraisal — tap the Pokémon, open the ⋮ menu, then Appraise.

Pokémon caught from Raids, hatched from Eggs, or earned via Field Research are guaranteed a minimum IV floor in every stat (commonly 10/15 or higher) — so they tend to be stronger on average than a random wild catch.

Each player starts with 6 face-down Pokémon. You can\'t see your own cards until you pick one — it\'s all about instinct.
